data.body: Parity gap (RP-record-parity-audit): api.records has record_merge, record_split, record_supersede and record_restore, but surfaces/declared/recordkinds.py VERBS stops at list show add edit remove search revise history, so no data kind can merge, split, supersede or restore from the CLI or MCP. Add the four verbs to the one declaration (VERBS, param choices, MCP description, dispatcher) so every kind gets them at once; no per-kind code. Then delete the @engine exemptions for merge, split, supersede and restore in ddflow/api/records/parity.py (the ratchet fails until you do).
data.title: Record surface: offer merge, split, supersede and restore on the generic record CLI and MCP tool, as the API already does

data.body: Parity gap (RP-record-parity-audit): only task update has --append-body; no record kind can append to a text field. Add one `append` verb to the shared verb set (api/records/_verbs.py and the surface declaration) that appends to a text field of any kind and logs it as an edit with the appended text, then delete the @engine append exemption in ddflow/api/records/parity.py. The legacy kinds get it when they move onto the engine (RP-engine-* tasks).
data.title: Record engine: an append verb (add text to a text field, keep the original) for every kind

data.body: Parity gap (RP-record-parity-audit, rule r-record-parity): this kind is not a RecordKind, so it lacks capabilities the shared engine gives every declared kind; the matrix is in docs/ddflow/research/record-parity.md and ddflow/api/records/parity.py lists it under LEGACY with an exemption naming this task. Declare it as a RecordKind (data descriptor, no per-kind verbs), keep its existing CLI words as aliases, preserve event-log compatibility, remove the LEGACY row and the exemption from ddflow/api/records/parity.py, and the parity test then covers it. Do not write per-kind special cases.
data.title: Move session notes and session records onto the shared RecordKind engine so create, edit, append, filter, revise, merge, split, delete, restore, history, search, recall, export and context come from one descriptor
